{{Quote|For years, Sith conquests in this region stalled due to infighting. Until only Chagras was left from his generation&mdash;and peace came.|Arkadia Calimondra|<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />}}
'''Chagras''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who became a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] during the [[Republic Dark Age]]. He was one of seven children of [[Vilia Calimondra]], a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] who had established a [[Vilia Calimondra's empire|large empire]] in the [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]], and he fought against his siblings in a [[Charge Matrica|contest]] to determine which one of them would become their [[Parent/Legends|mother's]] heir. During the war, he became the leader of a Sith state known as the [[Chagras Hegemony]] and gained control of large regions of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Chagras eventually emerged as the victor of the contest and became Calimondra's heir. In [[1042 BBY]], he launched a campaign against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], but before he could conquer many [[Planet/Legends|worlds]], he was [[Death/Legends|killed]] under unexplained circumstances in [[1040 BBY]] by a [[Nerve toxin/Legends|nerve toxin]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Chagras and Xelian were brother and sister&mdash;two of the seven children of Vilia Calimondra.|Arkadia Calimondra|<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />}}
[[File:Odionhead.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The Sith Lord Odion, a nephew of Chagras, fought under his uncle's banner.]]
Chagras was a [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Human" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> who lived during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Republic Dark Age]].<ref name="Dark Age">The StarWars.com article [http://www.starwars.com/vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''] states that the ''Knight Errant'' novel is set in 1032 BBY, and that Chagras died eight years before the events of the end of the novel. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' identifies this time frame as being part of the Republic Dark Age.</ref> He was one of seven children of [[Vilia Calimondra]], a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] who controlled a [[Vilia Calimondra's empire|large empire]] in the [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]], and he made a claim to become the heir to Calimondra's holdings. However, his siblings all made similar claims,<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> so, in [[1066 BBY]],<ref name="1066 BBY">The ''Knight Errant'' novel mentions that the ''Charge Matrica'' began 34 years before the events of the book. As the StarWars.com article [http://www.starwars.com/vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''] states that ''Knight Errant'' is set in 1032 BBY, this places the start of the contest in 1066 BBY.</ref> Calimondra instigated the ''[[Charge Matrica]]'', a contest designed to determine which of her children would be appointed as her beneficiary. She tasked her children with expanding her holdings, planning to make her heir the individual who expanded her territories the most, and, for a time, the siblings cooperated. However, after her bid began to flounder, Chagras' sister [[Xelian]] declared war on him, causing all of the siblings to initiate hostilities against each other.<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />

Through his cleverness, Chagras was able to gain control of large regions of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], forging a Sith state known as the [[Chagras Hegemony]].<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> At some point, he developed the [[Death Spiral]], a type of automated ground attack vehicle, and he constructed several of them. He [[Parent/Legends|fathered]] a daughter, [[Arkadia Calimondra]], and he also became an uncle to his siblings' various children, including Xelian's sons, [[Daiman]] and [[Odion]].<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> In circa [[1046 BBY]],<ref name="1046 BBY">The ''Knight Errant'' novel mentions that Dromika and Quillan were 14 years old during the events of the book. As the StarWars.com article [http://www.starwars.com/vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''] states that ''Knight Errant'' is set in 1032 BBY, this places their births in circa 1046 BBY.</ref> he became a father again, to the [[Twin/Legends|twins]] [[Dromika]] and [[Quillan (Sith)|Quillan]].<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />

Eventually, Chagras was the only one of Vilia Calimondra's children left, and he became her heir<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> at some point circa [[1050 BBY/Legends|1050 BBY]].<ref name="1050 BBY">The ''Knight Errant'' novel mentions that Kerra Holt was born during the period of peace that followed the conclusion of the ''Charge Matrica''. As the StarWars.com article [http://www.starwars.com/vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''] states that ''Knight Errant'' is set in 1032 BBY, and the novel states that Holt was 18 years old during the events of the book, this places the conclusion of the ''Charge Matrica'' at sometime before or during 1050 BBY.</ref> His victory brought a period of stability to the Grumani [[Sector/Legends|sector]] and guaranteed Chagras the assistance of his nieces and nephews, so he tasked them with repairing the damage that the war had caused his holdings.<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> By [[1042 BBY]],<ref name="1042 BBY">The [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Knight Errant 2|''Knight Errant: Aflame'' 2]] states that the attack on Aquilaris took place 10 years before the [[Star Wars: Knight Errant (comic series)|''Knight Errant'' comic series]], which, according to [[Knight Errant 0|''Knight Errant'' 0]], is set in 1032 BBY, thus dating the attack to 1042 BBY.</ref> he was strong enough to turn his attention to the [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], outside the bounds of the Grumani sector,<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> and he dispatched Odion to [[Raid on Sanbra|sack]] the [[University of Sanbra]],<ref name="Knight Errant 14">[[Knight Errant: Escape 4|''Knight Errant: Escape'' 4]]</ref> a famed educational establishment situated on the planet [[Sanbra]].<ref name="GG 12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> Shortly afterward,<ref name="Knight Errant 14" /> on the orders of Calimondra, Chagras sent Odion to [[Massacre of Aquilaris|conquer]] the Republic-held world [[Aquilaris]].<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> Odion massacred most of the world's inhabitants, and Chagras eventually intervened and prevented his nephew from killing all of the planet's population, so that some of the people could be used as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], to operate Aquilaris's [[Fleek eel/Legends|fleek eel]] traps.<ref name="Knight Errant 6">[[Knight Errant: Deluge 1|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 1]]</ref> Odion secretly captured some University of Sanbra researchers from Aquilaris to help him to track down the [[Helm of Ieldis]], a powerful [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifact]], and he suspected that the real reason why he had been sent away was because Chagras suspected something.<ref name="Knight Errant 14" /> Late in his reign, Chagras annexed the agrarian planet [[Chelloa]], and he relocated much of the world's population to the frontier regions of the Chagras Hegemony to fight for him. However, before many more planets could fall to the Sith, Chagras was [[Death/Legends|killed]]<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> under unexplained circumstances,<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> in [[1040 BBY]],<ref name="1040 BBY" /> by a powerful [[Nerve toxin/Legends|nerve toxin]].<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />

Following Chagras' death, custody of Dromika and Quillan passed to the [[Krevaaki]] [[Saaj Calician]], a Sith Lord who had previously served under Chagras. Vilia Calimondra began a [[Second Charge Matrica|second ''Charge Matrica'']] to find a replacement heir from among her grandchildren, and they soon went to war against each other, shattering Chagras' former holdings into more than ten different parts.<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> However, a small region of his territories held out from the invaders and became known as the [[Chagrasi Remnant]].<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" />

In circa [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]],<ref name="1032 BBY">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html|text=Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''}}</ref> the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vannar Treece]] compiled a report on the state of affairs in the Grumani sector, and in it he detailed Chagras' rise to power and subsequent death.<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> Around this time, Arkadia initiated a plot to avenge her father's death by murdering Vilia, whom she believed had arranged for his demise. Arkadia theorized that her grandmother had organized the ''Charge Matrica'' as a way of keeping the [[Calimondra family]] focused on fighting each other, rather than plotting against their matriarch, and that Vilia had lived in fear of [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] once Chagras had won the contest. Arkadia arranged to send the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Narsk Ka'hane]] to kill Vilia using [[Chagras's Blood]], a type of nerve toxin created from [[Synedian algae]]. However, Ka'hane was secretly an agent of Vilia, and Arkadia's plot was unsuccessful.<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|While no less bloodthirsty than his rivals, Chagras used cleverness to bring huge swaths of space under his control&mdash;and is still regarded by refugees who lived under his rule as the lesser of several evils.|Jedi Master Vannar Treece|<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" />}}
Chagras was a clever individual, and many refugees considered Chagras' rule to be preferable to life under some of the sector's other Sith.<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> He doted on Dromika and Quillan, and they found it difficult when he died. Chagras had the ability to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Force healing/Legends|heal]] himself, but the nerve toxin that killed him was too effective for his [[Force power/Legends|powers]] to overcome.<ref name="Knight Errant novel" />

==Behind the scenes==
Chagras was created by [[John Jackson Miller]] and first mentioned in [[Knight Errant 0|''Knight Errant'' 0]], a preview issue of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series [[Star Wars: Knight Errant (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knight Errant'']], which made reference to the "Chagras Hegemony."<ref name="Knight Errant 0">[[Knight Errant 0|''Knight Errant'' 0]]</ref> In [[November]] [[2010]], he received another mention, in [[The Knight Errant Gazetteer|The ''Knight Errant'' Gazetteer]], an article that was written by Miller, [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], and published on [[StarWars.com]]. The article was the first source to identify Chagras as a distinct individual, and it clarified the nature of his relationship to the Chagras Hegemony.<ref name="Knight Errant Gazetteer" /> He was later referenced in the [[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'' novel]], which was written by Miller and released in [[January]] [[2011]],<ref name="Knight Errant novel" /> and he received further mentions in the [[Knight Errant: Deluge 1|6th]]<ref name="Knight Errant 6" /> and [[Knight Errant: Escape 4|14th]] issues of the comic.<ref name="Knight Errant 14" />
